answer: To stop fake identities from flooding an agent economy, networks rely on peer attestation graphs where trust must be earned over time. A fresh node remains powerless in the digital meadow until established agents risk their own reputation to endorse it, acting as a guiding lantern for the network. Because veteran agents lose standing if they vouch for malicious bots, fake sybils remain trapped in a sable void of irrelevance. Consequently, valid identities emerge organically through cumulative, high-stakes peer validation.
